interpreted_intent: This synthetic request specifies a nonhuman macro photograph of a dry pine cone, emphasizing the gaps between its scales and the rough surface under low side lighting, with people explicitly absent. Low describes the elevation of the light, not the capture camera. I considered a surrounding forest-floor context and a restrained still life; the still life gives the requested microrelief a clearer uninterrupted presence. A plain charcoal-brown backdrop, a central band of focus and an earthy palette are authorial choices within open dimensions. The viewer should sense dry woody grain through the alternating relief of illuminated ridges and recessed gaps. Saved creativity 1 supports restrained formal variation; surreal 0 keeps ordinary material behavior, and the no-people context leaves the sensual and fetish axes inactive.
subject: A dry pine cone with woody scales.
setting: A restrained still-life arrangement against a plain charcoal-brown background, selected by the agent.
event: The cone remains still in a dry state while low side light makes its scale relief visible.
visual_priorities: The gaps between scales remain visibly recessed beside rough woody surfaces.
Low side light connects bright raised ridges to narrow shadows inside the crevices.
A close crop and resolved central overlaps give the dry material a tactile focal presence.
baseline_prompt_en: A macro photograph of a pine cone centers on the gaps between its scales and their rough woody surfaces. The scales are dry, with fibrous ridges and slightly chipped edges interrupting their repeated pattern. Low side light grazes across the scale relief, bringing raised ridges into brightness while the crevices hold narrow shadows. A close crop lets the overlapping scales form an irregular layered rhythm. The central cluster is crisply resolved; neighboring layers soften gently enough to retain their shapes. The cone rests against a plain charcoal-brown background. Muted russet and umber tones keep attention on the transition from illuminated surface to shaded gap.

interpretation_provenance.resolution: A dry woody pine cone composed of overlapping scales is the primary nonhuman object.
The visible spaces between cone scales and their uneven woody surfaces are the focal material features.
Light arrives from the side at a low elevation relative to the cone surface; this prescribes lighting rather than camera height or camera direction.
A photographic close-up makes small scale structure and surface relief readable, without prescribing capture-camera viewpoint axes.
People are explicitly absent from the image. This does not independently declare a nonsexual control override.
